subject: QBR Prep: OKR check-ins & consolidated pipeline snapshots
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: QBR Prep: OKR check-ins & consolidated pipeline snapshots

Team —

We need a tight, usable package for next week's QBR. Executive asks are straightforward: a consolidated forecast (workbook attached) plus concise account one-pagers for any deals >$100k expected in Q4. Specifics below — please treat as deliverables for your book of business.

Deliverables (due Tue 12/01 EOD):
- Updated row(s) in 2026Q4_forecast_master.xlsx (attached). Fill in committed ARR, expected close date, probability, and delta to prior forecast.
- One-pager (PDF) per account >$100k: 1 page, bullets: current ask, blockers, security/compliance items outstanding, next 2 steps, recommended exec ask. Attach to your reply.
- Risk flag per account: G/Y/R with 1-sentence rationale.

Ask for this thread: reply with status + attachments (or a link to the one-pagers). If you're owning Acme Analytics, include the procurement contact and any proposed concession request.

Context: execs want a per-account narrative (not just numbers) to go with the consolidated slides. Keep the tone factual and explicit about open asks or approvals needed from leadership during the QBR.

Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/u/0/folders/1QBR_Prep_2026
HubSpot master: HSP-234567

I attached the forecast master template to make consolidation faster. Ping me if you need a headcount/discount approval for a concession.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: 2026Q4_forecast_master.xlsx

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: QBR Prep: OKR check-ins & consolidated pipeline snapshots

Marissa — thanks for the clear ask. Quick status from my side for accounts I'm driving:

1) Acme Analytics (expected $210k ARR) — attached one-pager (acme_account_onepager.pdf). Current blocker: legal redline on data-retention and an outstanding SOC-2 evidence request. Procurement wants a single-seat POC contract in place before approving full purchase order. Risk: Y (expect close calendar week of 12/13 if legal signoff happens).

2) BrightFin (Mira Solis) — $160k ARR pipeline. They've requested latency SLO language for inference endpoints in the contract; engineering has proposed an SLA appendix. Risk: Y (need legal + SRE note).

3) MidMarketCo — $85k ARR (below threshold, excluding one-pager).

Notes/asks:
- I updated the forecast sheet with committed numbers and probability columns. See tab "Rishi_book".
- For Acme: procurement@acmeanalytics.com looped in on the one-pager. I'm attaching the exported procurement contact CSV (acme_procurement_export.csv) that procurement sent — includes billing contact and PO cadence.

Question: for concessions (discount or credit to offset integration cost) — do we want to route these as a central credit request or have each AE ask for approval ad-hoc? Prefer a single go/no-go from sales ops to keep QBR narrative consistent.

- Attachment: acme_account_onepager.pdf, acme_procurement_export.csv

Marissa / Rishi —

I've reviewed Rishi's Acme one-pager and the forecast inputs. I updated the master file with the delta column and included my assumptions in the "notes" cell (linked to Acme's HubSpot: HSP-234567). Summary:
- Acme Analytics: I moved the close date to 12/14 and set probability to 70% based on procurement timeline. Committed ARR (if signed) = $210k.
- BrightFin: moved probability to 60% pending SLA appendix.

Recommended exec ask for Acme: sign approval for SOC-2 evidence acceptance plan (we can provide a scoped excerpt of our SOC report and a commitment to provide redacted logs). If execs authorize a short-term acceptance path, procurement will accept initial PO.

Attaching Acme one-pager for inclusion in the package.

- Attachment: acme_account_onepager.pdf

Subject: Re: QBR Prep: OKR check-ins & consolidated pipeline snapshots

Looping in a couple of procurement/discount items I want leadership to be aware of before the QBR:

- Acme: they requested a one-time integration credit to offset an enterprise connector build. I recommend we consider a modest credit (5-7% of first-year ARR) if execs want a clean close in December. If we approve a credit, Sales Ops should show net ARR impact in the consolidated sheet.
- Policy: for any credit > $10k, we should route a formal approval to Finance + Legal.

DocuSign (draft concession): https://app.docusign.com/raft/doc/RD-CREDIT-ACME-2026 (internal preview only)

If folks want, I can prepare the short approval slide for the QBR packet.

Subject: Re: QBR Prep: OKR check-ins & consolidated pipeline snapshots

Thanks all — excellent, concise updates and attachments. Quick synthesis and next steps so the exec packet is ready on Friday: 

1) Consolidation: Rishi/Laura — I will merge your Acme numbers into the final sheet and include the one-pager in the QBR appendix. Karthik — please include the proposed concession on the approval slide and flag the Finance path if >$10k.
2) Exec asks: Approve SOC-2 acceptance plan (for Acme) and a one-time integration credit up to 7% for close-in-December.
3) Dry-run: Fri 12/04 at 11:00am PT — 30min run-through for the packet. Invite will follow.
4) Outstanding: Rishi to confirm procurement PO cadence (from acme_procurement_export.csv) and update close date if PO arrives earlier.

Attachments I'll publish to the folder shortly: consolidated_2026Q4_forecast.xlsx (master), QBR_appendix.zip (all one-pagers). If anyone has late edits, send them by Thu EOD.

Thanks for moving quickly — this will make the exec review crisp and actionable.

Marissa Cole
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: consolidated_2026Q4_forecast.xlsx, QBR_appendix.zip
